newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 1996 budget gap seen down at 2.5 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Polish 1996 budget gap seen down at 2.5 pct of GDP.

text.p: Poland is likely to end up with a budget deficit of about 2.5 percent of its gross domestic product this year against the 2.8 percent plan and last year's 2.7 percent, the head of the public debt department said.
Piotr Dziewulski told a news conference the gap was likely to be smaller than planned because of smaller costs of financing of the public debt.
"The deficit is likely to be about 2.5 percent because of smaller costs of financing of the domestic and foreign debt," Dziewulski said. @

"For instance, we expected that yields of T-bills would ease four percentage points in 1996 while in fact they fell as much as 5.5 points, which also reduced costs of the 10-year and three-year bonds which have coupons based on T-bills," he said.
"We have also sold more 52-week paper then planned, which shifts some of the debt to the next year," he added.
Polish budget deficit narrowed by about 1.5 billion zlotys to 4.91 billion zlotys in November, which accounted for 48.3 percent of the planned 1996 deficit of 10.16 billion zlotys.
